title: Memory, caches and locality

objectives.text: Derive flat row-major index traces and distinguish spatial/temporal locality from identity, correctness and a real speed measurement.
Analyze an explicitly bounded synthetic LRU line-cache model while separating model miss counts, real cache/TLB/page effects and measurement requirements.

blocks.markdown: Spatial locality means nearby addresses are accessed near one another in time; temporal locality means recently used data/instructions are reused. These are workload tendencies, not laws or correctness guarantees. A cache holds limited data/metadata closer to computation so an access may avoid a more expensive lower-level path. Cache hits/misses, allocations, branches, TLB translations and OS page faults are different events. This lesson explains access order and a synthetic model, not measured hardware speed.

A flat rows-by-cols array stored in row-major order maps cell(r,c)to offset r*cols+c. Consecutive c values give consecutive elements; consecutive r with fixed c steps by cols. With bounded 4-by-4 int values 0..15, both traversals below visit every element exactly once and sum 120. The sum is safely held in long long. std::array elements are contiguous; a vector-of-vectors does not make all rows one single contiguous allocation, and Python list elements are object references rather than a packed numeric matrix.

blocks.caption: Expected output: 120 120, then 6. The mapping(1,2)->6 and equal sums establish this bounded access contract, not which traversal runs faster. No timing, CPU line size, vectorization or cache counter is measured. App C++ runner remains unverified.

blocks.markdown: For reasoning, declare an aligned synthetic array with 4 ELEMENTS per cache line and 2 resident lines, fully associative, exact least-recently-used eviction, initially empty, demand read accesses only. This is not a claim that a hardware line contains 4 int values or that LRU/associativity/prefetch behave this way. Element index i maps to model line floor(i/4). A hit updates recency; a miss loads that line and evicts the oldest resident line if full. Each function call starts cold, so warm reuse must be included in the same trace.

blocks.title: Count declared model misses without inventing elapsed time

steps.text: Row-order trace 0,1,2,3,4,...,15 visits line 0 four times, then 1, then 2, then 3. Each line has one initial miss and 3 hits: 4 misses, 12 hits.
Column-order trace 0,4,8,12,1,5,... visits lines 0,1,2,3 repeatedly. A 2-line LRU cache evicts each needed line before reuse, producing 16 misses and 0 hits.

If capacity increases to 4 lines, row-order repeated twice has only the first 4 misses and 28 hits in 32 accesses. The second pass fits the model working set. Changing capacity/alignment/access pattern changes the count.

blocks.source:
def modeled_lru(trace, line_elements, capacity_lines):
    # Synthetic element-index trace; aligned base, fully associative exact LRU, demand loads only.
    if type(trace) is not list or len(trace)>10000 or any(type(i) is not int or not 0<=i<=1000000 for i in trace):
        raise ValueError("expected bounded integer element-index list")
    if type(line_elements) is not int or not 1<=line_elements<=1024 or type(capacity_lines) is not int or not 1<=capacity_lines<=1024:
        raise ValueError("expected bounded positive integer model geometry")
    resident=[] # oldest first; new independent cold cache each call
    hits=misses=0
    for index in trace:
        line=index//line_elements
        if line in resident:
            hits+=1
            resident.remove(line)
        else:
            misses+=1
            if len(resident)==capacity_lines:
                resident.pop(0)
        resident.append(line)
    return hits,misses

rows=cols=4
row_order=[r*cols+c for r in range(rows) for c in range(cols)]
column_order=[r*cols+c for c in range(cols) for r in range(rows)]
print(modeled_lru(row_order,4,2))
print(modeled_lru(column_order,4,2))
print(modeled_lru(row_order+row_order,4,4))
print(sorted(row_order)==sorted(column_order))
blocks.caption: Expected output: (12, 4), (0, 16), (28, 4), True. Hits+misses equals trace length and both orders have the same index multiset. The list-based LRU implementation is a transparent small bounded simulator, not constant-time cache hardware, a performance benchmark, or a promise about an actual CPU.

blocks.markdown: Real systems can have several cache levels, finite associativity, hardware prefetch, replacement approximations, write allocation/coherence, translation caches and multiple page sizes. Cache-line bytes and element size/alignment matter; do not hardcode a universal 64-byte line. A TLB caches address translations, not the same thing as a data-cache line; missing a translation cache is not automatically a disk page fault. Allocation and a large virtual address range do not imply all pages are physically resident.

Before comparing real speed, verify equal work/results, define input sizes/layout/distribution, toolchain/flags/hardware/runtime, warm/cold/setup/I-O boundaries and counter semantics. Prevent the optimizer from eliminating unused results without introducing a new workload; use proper measurement tools and retain observable results. Repeat measurements and report dispersion/tail behavior. A toy model or one noisy elapsed time cannot certify low-latency production behavior. Later profiling lessons develop an actual measurement protocol.

Independent transfer: generate row/column traces for bounded rectangular shapes, verify both are permutations of the full offset range, and compare exact model counts to an independently implemented recency reference. Include empty traces, repeated single-line access, a capacity fitting the working set and a cycle with one more line than capacity. Explain why a model count can change without an algorithm changing its mathematical answer.

Sources: [OSTEP TLB/locality examples](https://pages.cs.wisc.edu/~remzi/OSTEP/vm-tlbs.pdf), [replacement/locality policy](https://pages.cs.wisc.edu/~remzi/OSTEP/vm-beyondphys-policy.pdf), and [ordinary vector storage contracts](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/container/vector.html). Textbook historical timings/CPU examples are not imported as current universal hardware facts. Own line geometry is deliberately synthetic.

summary: Access correctness and locality are different. Derive layout/trace first, state model geometry and cold/warm policy, then treat modeled hits/misses as model results rather than measured real hardware speed or production qualification.
